answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by requiring each identity to continuously verify unique crystal formation rates in monitored orchard environments under varying gale conditions. The mechanism operates through agents submitting cryptographically signed, timestamped sensor readings that must match independent physical measurements; an attacker creating multiple fake identities would need to either deploy costly physical sensors at scale or forge consistent multi-source data, both of which make the economic cost of Sybil farming exceed potential gains from any individual account.
